topics.label: Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets the context within the cancer course, and outlines the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Concepts of Cancer Causation: Genetics, Environment, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolving genetic disease and evaluate the relative contributions of intrinsic biological errors versus environmental exposures through global epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive malignancy, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study of pathogen-induced oncogenesis.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how specific environmental mutagens and metabolic activation pathways cause direct DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumour Promoters, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the two-stage carcinogenesis model by differentiating non-mutagenic promoters and inflammatory microenvironments from initiators across varying host developmental stages.

topics.label: Methodologies for Assessing and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the scientific methodologies employed to detect carcinogens and establish their causal link to cancer, including mutational signatures, biobanks, animal models, and in vitro tests.

topics.label: Conclusion: Risk Assessment and Summary
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic synthesizes the lecture's key insights on environmental carcinogenicity and reflects on everyday risk-benefit decisions.
